hindi: अब, इसलिए, हम 'आरग्वधीय' अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter called Āragvadhīya (the chapter relating to āragvadha).
notes: Standard opening formula. 'Āragvadhīya' is named after the first drug mentioned, āragvadha.
lines_iast: athāta āragvadhīyamadhyāyaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ
lines_deva: अथात आरग्वधीयमध्यायं व्याख्यास्यामः

hindi: ऐसा निश्चय ही भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus, indeed, spoke the venerable Ātreya.
notes: 'iti ha smāha' is a fixed formula of reported speech; the particles ha and sma add no separate sense beyond 'indeed, (so) said'.
lines_iast: iti ha smāha bhagavānātreyaḥ
lines_deva: इति ह स्माह भगवानात्रेयः

hindi: आरग्वध (एडगज के साथ), करञ्ज, वासा, गुडूची, मदन, दोनों हरिद्राएँ; 'श्री' नामक, 'सुर' नामक, खदिर और धव, निम्ब, विडङ्ग, करवीरक की छाल।
english: Āragvadha together with eḍagaja, karañja, vāsā, guḍūcī, madana, the two haridrās; the one named Śrī, the one named Sura, khadira and dhava, nimba, viḍaṅga, the bark of karavīraka.
notes: Drug list; the verse contains no verb. The sentence is completed in verse 6 (the six half-verses are six powder groups; each printed line here is one group). 'saiḍagajaḥ' = sa + eḍagaja; it may belong to āragvadha (as translated) or be read with karañja (cf. unit 15 'saiḍagajaḥ karañjaḥ'). 'haridre' is dual (two haridrās); the text does not say which two. 'śryāhvaḥ' and 'surāhvaḥ' are descriptive names ('called Śrī', 'called Sura'); identification is left to commentators, none is asserted here.
lines_iast: āragvadhaḥ saiḍagajaḥ karañjo vāsā guḍūcī madanaṃ haridre
śryāhvaḥ surāhvaḥ khadiro dhavaśca nimbo viḍaṅgaṃ karavīrakatvak
lines_deva: आरग्वधः सैडगजः करञ्जो वासा गुडूची मदनं हरिद्रे
श्र्याह्वः सुराह्वः खदिरो धवश्च निम्बो विडङ्गं करवीरकत्वक्

hindi: और ग्रन्थि, भौर्ज, लहसुन, शिरीष लोमश के साथ, गुग्गुलु और कृष्णगन्धा, फणिज्झक, वत्सक और सप्तपर्ण, पीलु, कुष्ठ तथा सुमनस् की कोंपलें।
english: And granthi, bhaurja, garlic, śirīṣa together with lomaśa, guggulu and kṛṣṇagandhā, phaṇijjhaka, vatsaka and saptaparṇa, pīlus, kuṣṭha, and sumanas shoots.
notes: Drug list (continues from unit 3). Meanings uncertain without commentary: granthi, bhaurja, lomaśa, kṛṣṇagandhā, phaṇijjhaka are kept as names. 'salomaśaḥ' could also be read as an adjective 'hairy'; here read sa + lomaśa as in unit 15. 'guggulukṛṣṇagandhe' read as a dual dvandva 'guggulu and kṛṣṇagandhā' (ending -e); it could be a neuter dual or a feminine dual. 'pīlūni' is a neuter plural of pīlu (commentators may read fruits). 'sumanas' is kept as is (a general word for flower; jasmine per commentators).
lines_iast: granthiśca bhaurjo laśunaḥ śirīṣaḥ salomaśo guggulukṛṣṇagandhe
phaṇijjhako vatsakasaptaparṇau pīlūni kuṣṭhaṃ sumanaḥpravālāḥ
lines_deva: ग्रन्थिश्च भौर्जो लशुनः शिरीषः सलोमशो गुग्गुलुकृष्णगन्धे
फणिज्झको वत्सकसप्तपर्णौ पीलूनि कुष्ठं सुमनःप्रवालाः

hindi: वचा, हरेणु, त्रिवृता, निकुम्भ, भल्लातक, गैरिक और अञ्जन; मनःशिला और आल, गृहधूम (घर का धुआँ; कालिख के अर्थ में), इलायची (एला), कासीस, लोध्र, अर्जुन, मुस्त और सर्ज।
english: Vacā, hareṇu, trivṛtā, nikumbha, bhallātaka, gairika and añjana; manaḥśilā and āla, house-smoke (gṛhadhūma; understood as soot), elā (cardamom), kāśīsa, lodhra, arjuna, musta and sarja.
notes: Drug list (continues). 'manaḥśilāle' read as dual dvandva manaḥśilā + āla (the usual pair; āla taken as orpiment, an identification not stated in the verse). 'gṛhadhūma' is literally 'house-smoke'; understood as household soot. 'kāśīsa' read as one word (a mineral), not kāśī + sa-.
lines_iast: vacā hareṇustrivṛtā nikumbho bhallātakaṃ gairikamañjanaṃ ca
manaḥśilāle gṛhadhūma elā kāśīsalodhrārjunamustasarjāḥ
lines_deva: वचा हरेणुस्त्रिवृता निकुम्भो भल्लातकं गैरिकमञ्जनं च
मनःशिलाले गृहधूम एला काशीसलोध्रार्जुनमुस्तसर्जाः

hindi: इस प्रकार आधे-आधे श्लोक के रूप में बताए गए ये छह (योग), गाय के पित्त में भिगोए हुए और फिर पीसे हुए, इसके बाद तैयार किए हुए तथा सरसों के तेल से युक्त चूर्ण-प्रदेह के रूप में वैद्य द्वारा प्रयोग किए जाने चाहिए।
english: These six, thus set out in half-verse forms, soaked in cow's bile and then ground again, afterwards prepared and combined with mustard oil, are to be applied by the physician as powder-pastes (cūrṇa-pradeha).
notes: 'ardharūpa': 'half-verse forms'; the six are the six printed lines of units 3 to 5, each a drug group. 'pīta' literally 'drunk', i.e. imbibed or soaked. 'siddha' is ambiguous (prepared, cooked, finished); rendered 'prepared'. 'param' may also mean 'excellent'; taken as 'afterwards'. The text does not say how long the soaking or the method of preparation.
lines_iast: ityardharūpairvihitāḥ ṣaḍete gopittapītāḥ punareva piṣṭāḥ
siddhāḥ paraṃ sarṣapatailayuktāścūrṇapradehā bhiṣajā prayojyāḥ
lines_deva: इत्यर्धरूपैर्विहिताः षडेते गोपित्तपीताः पुनरेव पिष्टाः
सिद्धाः परं सर्षपतैलयुक्ताश्चूर्णप्रदेहा भिषजा प्रयोज्याः

hindi: प्रयोग किए जाने पर ये (योग) मनुष्यों के कठिन कुष्ठों, नए किलास, सुरेशलुप्त (इन्द्रलुप्त), दद्रु-सहित किटिभ, भगन्दर, अर्श तथा पामा-सहित अपची को शीघ्र नष्ट कर सकते हैं।
english: Applied, they would quickly destroy in people: difficult kuṣṭhas, recent kilāsa, sureśalupta (Indralupta), kiṭibha together with dadru, bhagandara, piles (arśas), and apacī together with pāmā.
notes: Subject (the six powder-pastes) is carried over from unit 6. 'navaṃ' is singular, so taken with kilāsa ('recent kilāsa'); 'kṛcchrāṇi' (plural) with kuṣṭhāni. 'sureśa-lupta' = Indra-lupta: sura-īśa = Indra. Disease names are kept in Sanskrit; the glosses are conventional and not stated in the verse. The sa- in 'sadadru' and 'sapāmāṃ' means 'together with'.
lines_iast: kuṣṭhāni kṛcchrāṇi navaṃ kilāsaṃ sureśaluptaṃ kiṭibhaṃ sadadru
bhagandarārśāṃsyapacīṃ sapāmāṃ hanyuḥ prayuktāstvacirānnarāṇām
lines_deva: कुष्ठानि कृच्छ्राणि नवं किलासं सुरेशलुप्तं किटिभं सदद्रु
भगन्दरार्शांस्यपचीं सपामां हन्युः प्रयुक्तास्त्वचिरान्नराणाम्

hindi: कुष्ठ, दोनों हरिद्राएँ, सुरस, पटोल, नीम और अश्वगन्धा, सुरदारु और शिग्रु, सरसों सहित, तुम्बुरु, धान्य, वन्य और चण्डा — इनके समान (बराबर) चूर्ण बनाने चाहिए।
english: One should make equal powders of kuṣṭha, the two haridrās, surasa, paṭola, nimba and aśvagandhā, suradāru and śigru, together with mustard, tumburu, dhānya, vanya and caṇḍā.
notes: 'tumburudhānyavanyaṃ' is read as a three-member dvandva; 'vanya' (literally 'wild') might instead qualify dhānya; commentarial identification needed. 'samāni' (equal) is not specified further (equal to each other); no quantity is given. 'suradāru' is literally 'god-wood'. Verse 8 begins a second formulation (powder, ground with buttermilk, rubbed on).
lines_iast: kuṣṭhaṃ haridre surasaṃ paṭolaṃ nimbāśvagandhe suradāruśigrū
sasarṣapaṃ tumburudhānyavanyaṃ caṇḍāṃ ca cūrṇāni samāni kuryāt
lines_deva: कुष्ठं हरिद्रे सुरसं पटोलं निम्बाश्वगन्धे सुरदारुशिग्रू
ससर्षपं तुम्बुरुधान्यवन्यं चण्डां च चूर्णानि समानि कुर्यात्

hindi: पहले तेल लगे हुए शरीर पर, मट्ठे (तक्र) के साथ पीसे हुए उन (चूर्णों) से उद्वर्तन (रगड़ना) करने का प्रयत्न करे। उससे इसकी खुजली, कोठ-सहित फुंसियाँ, कुष्ठ और सूजन शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: First, one should strive to rub the oil-smeared body with those (powders), ground with buttermilk. By that, his itching, boils together with koṭha rashes, kuṣṭhas and swellings go to rest.
notes: 'taiḥ' refers back to the powders of the preceding units (here, of unit 8 at least). 'asya' read as 'his' (the patient's). 'udvartana' is a rubbing or scrubbing treatment. 'koṭha' is kept as a name for a rash of raised wheals. 'kaṇḍūḥ' is singular with a plural verb, as the subject is a list.
lines_iast: taistakrapiṣṭaiḥ prathamaṃ śarīraṃ tailāktamudvartayituṃ yateta
tenāsyakaṇḍūḥ piḍakāḥ sakoṭhāḥ kuṣṭhāni śophāśca śamaṃ vrajanti
lines_deva: तैस्तक्रपिष्टैः प्रथमं शरीरं तैलाक्तमुद्वर्तयितुं यतेत
तेनास्यकण्डूः पिडकाः सकोठाः कुष्ठानि शोफाश्च शमं व्रजन्ति

words.gram: last member of dvandva, m. nom. pl.

hindi: कुष्ठ, अमृतासङ्ग, कटङ्कटेरी, कासीस, कम्पिल्लक, मुस्त और लोध्र; सौगन्धिक, सर्ज का रस, विडङ्ग, मनःशिला और आल, तथा करवीरक की छाल।
english: Kuṣṭha, amṛtāsaṅga, kaṭaṅkaṭerī, kāsīsa, kampillaka, musta and lodhra; saugandhika, the resin of sarja, viḍaṅga, manaḥśilā and āla, and the bark of karavīraka.
notes: Drug list (continues; the third formulation, a set of powders used for dusting, see unit 11). 'kuṣṭhāmṛtāsaṅga-...' is one long compound. 'amṛtāsaṅga' is kept as one name; it could instead be divided amṛtā (guḍūcī) + saṅga, which is uncertain. 'sarjarasa' taken as the resin/sap of sarja (m. nom. sg. as a drug). 'saugandhika' not identified.
lines_iast: kuṣṭhāmṛtāsaṅgakaṭaṅkaṭerīkāsīsakampillakamustalodhrāḥ
saugandhikaṃ sarjaraso viḍaṅgaṃ manaḥśilāle karavīrakatvak
lines_deva: कुष्ठामृतासङ्गकटङ्कटेरीकासीसकम्पिल्लकमुस्तलोध्राः
सौगन्धिकं सर्जरसो विडङ्गं मनःशिलाले करवीरकत्वक्

words.gloss: of one whose body is smeared with oil

hindi: तेल लगे शरीर वाले (व्यक्ति) पर इन बनाए हुए चूर्णों को अवचूर्णन के लिए लगाना चाहिए। इस प्रकार खुजली-सहित दद्रु, किटिभ, पामा और विचर्चिका भी शान्त हो जाते हैं।
english: One should apply these prepared powders, for dusting, on one whose body is smeared with oil. Thus dadru with itching, kiṭibha, pāmā and also vicarcikā come to rest.
notes: 'avacūrṇana' = sprinkling or dusting with powder. The verb 'eti' is singular; the plural list is treated as a group. Which powders ('etāni') are meant is not stated here (the groups of unit 10 are the nearest); read with units 9 and 10.
lines_iast: tailāktagātrasya kṛtāni cūrṇānyetāni dadyādavacūrṇanārtham
dadrūḥ sakaṇḍūḥ kiṭibhāni pāmā vicarcikā caiva tathaiti śāntim
lines_deva: तैलाक्तगात्रस्य कृतानि चूर्णान्येतानि दद्यादवचूर्णनार्थम्
दद्रूः सकण्डूः किटिभानि पामा विचर्चिका चैव तथैति शान्तिम्

hindi: मनःशिला, आल, काली मिर्च, तेल और अर्क का दूध (पयः) — यह कुष्ठ को दूर करने वाला प्रदेह है। इसी प्रकार तुत्थ, विडङ्ग, मिर्च, कुष्ठ और लोध्र मनःशिला के साथ (प्रदेह) हो।
english: Manaḥśilā, āla, peppers, oil and the milk (payas) of arka: this is a pradeha that removes kuṣṭha. Likewise, tuttha, viḍaṅga, peppers, kuṣṭha and lodhra should be (a pradeha) with manaḥśilā.
notes: 'ārkam payaḥ' = 'milk of arka'; arka is left unidentified (it has several senses). The second line has no stated subject; 'pradeha' is understood from line 1, 'likewise ... with manaḥśilā'. 'maricāni' (plural neuter) = peppers or peppercorns.
lines_iast: manaḥśilāle maricāni tailamārkaṃ payaḥ kuṣṭhaharaḥ pradehaḥ
tutthaṃ viḍaṅgaṃ maricāni kuṣṭhaṃ lodhraṃ ca tadvat samanaḥśilaṃ syāt
lines_deva: मनःशिलाले मरिचानि तैलमार्कं पयः कुष्ठहरः प्रदेहः
तुत्थं विडङ्गं मरिचानि कुष्ठं लोध्रं च तद्वत् समनःशिलं स्यात्

hindi: प्रपुनाड के बीजों सहित रसाञ्जन, कपित्थ के रस से मिलाया हुआ, लेप है। करञ्ज के बीज और एडगज, कुष्ठ के साथ, गोमूत्र में पीसे हुए — यह एक और (दूसरा) प्रदेह है।
english: Rasāñjana with prapunāḍa seeds, mixed with the juice of kapittha (wood-apple), is a lepa (plaster). Karañja seeds and eḍagaja, together with kuṣṭha, ground in cow's urine, are another pradeha.
notes: 'paraḥ' could mean 'another' (as rendered) or 'excellent'. 'karañjabījaiḍagajaṃ' = karañja-bīja + eḍagaja; eḍagaja may be the plant or its seeds. 'rasena' = with the juice (of the wood-apple fruit pulp). 'prapunāḍa' is as in the edition (metre requires short pu); the spelling prapunnāḍa also occurs elsewhere.
lines_iast: rasāñjanaṃ saprapunāḍabījaṃ yuktaṃ kapitthasya rasena lepaḥ
karañjabījaiḍagajaṃ sakuṣṭhaṃ gomūtrapiṣṭaṃ ca paraḥ pradehaḥ
lines_deva: रसाञ्जनं सप्रपुनाडबीजं युक्तं कपित्थस्य रसेन लेपः
करञ्जबीजैडगजं सकुष्ठं गोमूत्रपिष्टं च परः प्रदेहः

hindi: दोनों हरिद्राएँ, कुटज का बीज, करञ्ज का बीज, सुमनस् की कोंपलें, और हयमारक की छाल उसके मध्य भाग सहित — (इनसे) तिल के क्षार से युक्त लेप बनाना चाहिए।
english: One should prepare a lepa of both haridrās, the seed of kuṭaja, karañja seed, sumanas shoots, and the bark of hayamāraka together with its middle part, mixed with tila-kṣāra (sesame alkali).
notes: The accusatives (ubhe haridre ... pravālān, tvacam) are the ingredients; 'lepam' is the object of 'vidadhyāt'. Taken as one lepa of all listed items. 'samadhyāṃ' (f.) read with 'tvacam': 'bark with its middle (inner) part'; could mean something else. 'hayamāraka' literally 'horse-killer'; the identity is left to commentators. 'tilakṣāra' = alkali (ash-lye) from sesame, as read.
lines_iast: ubhe haridre kuṭajasya bījaṃ karañjabījaṃ sumanaḥpravālān
tvacaṃ samadhyāṃ hayamārakasya lepaṃ tilakṣārayutaṃ vidadhyāt
lines_deva: उभे हरिद्रे कुटजस्य बीजं करञ्जबीजं सुमनःप्रवालान्
त्वचं समध्यां हयमारकस्य लेपं तिलक्षारयुतं विदध्यात्

hindi: मनःशिला; कुष्ठ-सहित कुटज की छाल; लोमश और एडगज के साथ करञ्ज; ग्रन्थि और भौर्ज; और करवीर की जड़ — इनके चूर्ण तुषोदक (भूसी के जल) से तैयार किए जाने चाहिए।
english: Manaḥśilā; the bark of kuṭaja together with kuṣṭha; karañja with lomaśa and eḍagaja; granthi and bhaurja; and the root of karavīra: these powders are to be prepared with tuṣodaka (husk-water).
notes: The case endings of the first line (kuṭajāt sakuṣṭhāt, ablative) are unusual; read as 'bark from kuṭaja, with kuṣṭha'. 'saiḍagajaḥ karañjaḥ' could be 'karañja with eḍagaja' (as rendered) or 'eḍagaja and karañja'. 'sādhyāni' (to be accomplished/prepared) may also mean 'to be cooked'. Whether 'tuṣodaka' is plain husk-water or a fermented preparation is not stated here.
lines_iast: manaḥśilā tvak kuṭajāt sakuṣṭhāt salomaśaḥ saiḍagajaḥ karañjaḥ
granthiśca bhaurjaḥ karavīramūlaṃ cūrṇāni sādhyāni tuṣodakena
lines_deva: मनःशिला त्वक् कुटजात् सकुष्ठात् सलोमशः सैडगजः करञ्जः
ग्रन्थिश्च भौर्जः करवीरमूलं चूर्णानि साध्यानि तुषोदकेन

hindi: पलाश के निर्दाह (जले हुए अवशेष, भस्म) के रस से, जो एक आढक की मात्रा का हो, तथा कर्ष (के माप) से निकाले गए (पूर्व श्लोक के चूर्णों) से युक्त इस लेप को 'दर्वी-प्रलेप' कहते हैं; इस लेप को कुष्ठ का नाश करने के लिए श्रेष्ठ बताते हैं।
english: With the liquid (rasa) of palāśa-nirdāha (burnt matter of palāśa), measuring an āḍhaka, and with [the powders of the preceding verse] taken out by the karṣa (measure), they call this application darvī-pralepa, supreme for destroying kuṣṭha (obstinate skin disease).

text_flags.why: possible, spelling only: the usual spelling after ni- is niṣūdana (ṣ); may be edition spelling.

notes: Parsing is uncertain in places. (1) palāśa-nirdāha-rasa: nirdāha taken as 'burnt residue/ash' (so the liquid made from palāśa ash); 'the juice/extract of burnt palāśa' is the same idea; the text does not say how the liquid is made. (2) karṣoddhṛtāni (n. pl.) has no noun in this verse; it agrees with cūrṇāni of verse 15 (as the context suggests; verse 15 is not in this chunk); 'uddhṛta' may mean 'taken out/measured out at one karṣa each'. (3) darvī is kept as the name (not identified). (4) pravadanti ... lepam etam: double accusative, 'they call this lepa the darvī-pralepa'; the alternative 'they declare the darvī-pralepa, this lepa, supreme' gives the same sense. (5) kuṣṭha here is the disease (nisūdana = destroy); in other verses of the chunk kuṣṭha is a drug.
lines_iast: palāśanirdāharasena cāpi karṣoddhṛtānyāḍhakasaṃmitena
darvīpralepaṃ pravadanti lepametaṃ paraṃ kuṣṭhanisūdanāya
lines_deva: पलाशनिर्दाहरसेन चापि कर्षोद्धृतान्याढकसंमितेन
दर्वीप्रलेपं प्रवदन्ति लेपमेतं परं कुष्ठनिसूदनाय

words.gram: m./n. gen. sg. (bahuvrīhi: whose body is oil-anointed)

hindi: चतुरङ्गुल के पत्तों को तक्र (छाछ) के साथ पीसकर, फिर काकमाची के पत्तों को (भी पीसकर), तेल लगे हुए शरीर वाले मनुष्य के कुष्ठों का उद्वर्तन (उबटन की तरह मलना) करे; और अश्वहन के पत्तों से भी (करे)।
english: Having ground the leaves of caturaṅgula with buttermilk, and then the leaves of kākamācī, one should rub down the kuṣṭhas of a man whose body is anointed with oil, and also with leaves of aśvahana.
notes: The names caturaṅgula, kākamācī and aśvahana are kept as given; the text does not identify them here (caturaṅgula is traditionally a name of āragvadha and aśvahana of karavīra, not stated in the verse). 'piṣṭvā takreṇa' could also be read as grinding with buttermilk only the first set of leaves; the second 'parṇāni' is taken as also ground (understood). 'udvartayet' with kuṣṭhāni as object: rub/scrub off or rub over the kuṣṭhas. The last pāda adds a further means (instrumental): 'also with leaves of aśvahana'; the verse does not say how they are used.
lines_iast: parṇāni piṣṭvā caturaṅgulasya takreṇa parṇānyatha kākamācyāḥ
tailāktagātrasya narasya kuṣṭhānyudvartayedaśvahanacchadaiśca
lines_deva: पर्णानि पिष्ट्वा चतुरङ्गुलस्य तक्रेण पर्णान्यथ काकमाच्याः
तैलाक्तगात्रस्य नरस्य कुष्ठान्युद्वर्तयेदश्वहनच्छदैश्च

words.gloss: oil (member of taila-phala; tat-puruṣa or separate dvandva member, undecided)

hindi: कोल, कुलत्थ, सुरदारु, रास्ना, माष, अतसी, तैल-फल, कुष्ठ, वचा, शताह्वा, जौ का चूर्ण और खट्टा (पदार्थ) - ये गरम (हों तो) वातरोगियों के लिए प्रदेह हैं।
english: Kola, kulattha (horse-gram), suradāru, rāsnā, māṣa, atasī, taila-phalāni, kuṣṭha, vacā, śatāhvā, barley flour and the sour (amla): these, warm, are a pradeha (medicinal paste) for those afflicted with vāta disorders.

text_flags.why: Line has 21 syllables instead of 22; 'phāni' looks like a lost 'la' (phalāni), giving 22 and the usual word phala.

notes: The source reads 'tailaphāni' (one syllable short: 21 for the line). 'tailaphalāni' restores 22 and gives a word; read so. 'taila-phala' is kept as a name: it may be a drug called taila-phala, or 'taila' (oil) and 'phalāni' (fruits) separately; not decided. kola is usually jujube (badara) and māṣa black gram, atasī flax, but these are not glossed in the verse. 'amlam' is left as 'sour (substance)'. uṣṇāni (n. pl.) agrees with the whole list. kuṣṭha here is the drug.
lines_iast: kolaṃ kulatthāḥ suradārurāsnāmāṣātasītailaphāni kuṣṭham
vacā śatāhvā yavacūrṇamamlamuṣṇāni vātāmayināṃ pradehaḥ
lines_deva: कोलं कुलत्थाः सुरदारुरास्नामाषातसीतैलफानि कुष्ठम्
वचा शताह्वा यवचूर्णमम्लमुष्णानि वातामयिनां प्रदेहः

hindi: मछली और दलदली (अनूप) प्राणियों के मांस से बने गरम वेसवारों के साथ किया गया प्रदेह वायु को हरने वाला होता है। चार स्नेहों से, दशमूल से मिश्रित, तथा सुगन्धित औषधियों से (बना) प्रदेह वात का नाश करने वाला है।
english: A pradeha made with warm vesavāras (spiced boneless meat preparations) of the flesh of marsh-dwelling animals and of fish would remove Vāta; and a pradeha mixed with four fats (snehas), the daśamūla (the ten roots) and fragrant drugs destroys Vāta.
notes: ānūpa-matsya-āmiṣa is read as 'flesh of marsh-dwelling [animals] and fish'; the alternative 'flesh of marsh fish' is also grammatically possible. vesavāra is a spiced boneless-meat preparation (standard meaning). The 'four snehas' are not named in this verse (they are named elsewhere in the text), so they are not listed here. daśamūla is the standard group name for ten roots. In the second half 'pradehaḥ' may also be construed with the first half (the two halves each define a vāta-destroying pradeha).
lines_iast: ānūpamatsyāmiṣavesavārairuṣṇaiḥ pradehaḥ pavanāpahaḥ syāt
snehaiścaturbhirdaśamūlamiśrairgandhauṣadhaiścānilahaḥ pradehaḥ
lines_deva: आनूपमत्स्यामिषवेसवारैरुष्णैः प्रदेहः पवनापहः स्यात्
स्नेहैश्चतुर्भिर्दशमूलमिश्रैर्गन्धौषधैश्चानिलहः प्रदेहः

hindi: जौ का गरम चूर्ण, तक्र (छाछ) से युक्त और क्षार सहित, उदर (जठर) में होने वाली पीड़ा का नाश करे। वात में कुष्ठ, वचा सहित शताह्वा, और जौ का चूर्ण तेल व खट्टे पदार्थ के साथ (काम में लेना) अभीष्ट मानते हैं।
english: Warm barley flour combined with buttermilk and with alkali (kṣāra) would destroy pain in the abdomen. In Vāta they prescribe kuṣṭha, śatāhvā with vacā, and flour of barley, with oil and something sour.
notes: jaṭhare artim: 'pain in the abdomen'; jaṭhara could also be read as the disease name jaṭhara, but 'in the belly' is the plain reading. 'uśanti' (√vaś) is rendered 'they prescribe/approve'. The second half does not say 'pradeha' or 'external application' explicitly; the context (verses 18-19) suggests it, but the verse itself lists only the substances and 'vāte'. 'sakṣāram' agrees with yavacūrṇam.
lines_iast: takreṇa yuktaṃ yavacūrṇamuṣṇaṃ sakṣāramartiṃ jaṭhare nihanyāt
kuṣṭhaṃ śatāhvāṃ savacāṃ yavānāṃ cūrṇaṃ satailāmlamuśanti vāte
lines_deva: तक्रेण युक्तं यवचूर्णमुष्णं सक्षारमर्तिं जठरे निहन्यात्
कुष्ठं शताह्वां सवचां यवानां चूर्णं सतैलाम्लमुशन्ति वाते

words.gram: m. loc. sg. (bahuvrīhi), agreeing with pavane

hindi: दोनों शताह्वा, मधुक, मधूक, बला, प्रियाल और कशेरुक, घृत, विदारी और मिश्री - इनसे रक्त-सहित वात में प्रदेह करे।
english: Both śatāhvās, madhuka, madhūka, balā, priyāla and kaśeruka, ghee, vidārī and sugar-crystal (rock sugar): with these one should make a pradeha in Vāta accompanied by blood (rakta).
notes: 'ubhe śatāhve' = the two kinds of śatāhvā (not named in the verse). 'sarakte' is read as 'accompanied by rakta' (Vāta with blood involvement); it is not identified here with any named disease. 'sitopalā' = white crystal/lump, i.e. rock sugar. The other plant names are kept without identification (madhuka and madhūka are different words).
lines_iast: ubhe śatāhve madhukaṃ madhūkaṃ balāṃ priyālaṃ ca kaśerukaṃ ca
ghṛtaṃ vidārīṃ ca sitopalāṃ ca kuryāt pradehaṃ pavane sarakte
lines_deva: उभे शताह्वे मधुकं मधूकं बलां प्रियालं च कशेरुकं च
घृतं विदारीं च सितोपलां च कुर्यात् प्रदेहं पवने सरक्ते

hindi: रास्ना, गुडूची, मधुक, दोनों बला, जीवक तथा ऋषभक सहित और दूध, तथा सिद्ध किया हुआ घृत, मधुशेष से युक्त - प्रदेह रक्त और वायु की पीड़ा को दूर करे।
english: Rāsnā, guḍūcī, madhuka, the two balās, together with jīvaka and with ṛṣabhaka, and milk, and ghee that has been cooked (siddha), joined with madhuśeṣa: this pradeha would drive out the pain of blood and Vāta.
notes: 'madhuśeṣa' is uncertain: literally 'remainder of honey' (it might also be read as 'madhu' and 'śeṣa' separately, or as another substance such as what remains of honey); kept literal. 'siddham' = cooked/prepared; the verse does not say with what the ghee is cooked (presumably the listed drugs and milk, not stated). 'dve bale' = two balās (not named). 'raktānilārtim' = pain (ārti) of rakta and anila, or 'pain from blood and wind'; the compound could be 'rakta-anila-ārti' (dvandva then tat-puruṣa). guḍūcī is left as a name in the gloss.
lines_iast: rāsnā guḍūcī madhukaṃ bale dve sajīvakaṃ sarṣabhakaṃ payaśca
ghṛtaṃ ca siddhaṃ madhuśeṣayuktaṃ raktānilārtiṃ praṇudet pradehaḥ
lines_deva: रास्ना गुडूची मधुकं बले द्वे सजीवकं सर्षभकं पयश्च
घृतं च सिद्धं मधुशेषयुक्तं रक्तानिलार्तिं प्रणुदेत् प्रदेहः

words.gram: m. loc. sg. (sa-rakta, agreeing with vāte)

hindi: रक्त-सहित वात में गेहूँ के आटे का घृत-सहित प्रदेह (करे), और बकरी का दूध। सिर के दर्द में नत और उत्पल, चन्दन और कुष्ठ से युक्त, घृत सहित प्रदेह (करे)।
english: In Vāta accompanied by blood, a pradeha of wheat flour with ghee and with goat's milk; in headache, nata and utpala joined with candana and kuṣṭha, with ghee, as a pradeha.
notes: In the first half 'pradehaḥ' is the subject, 'saghṛtam' goes with the wheat flour. The second half has its own pradeha for śiro-rujā (head pain). 'nata' could be an adjective 'bent', but in a list of drugs it is taken as a drug name (kept). 'natotpalam' is a dvandva (nata and utpala) in the neuter singular; the other reading (nata-utpala as one named drug) is not excluded. The verb is understood in both halves.
lines_iast: vāte sarakte saghṛtaṃ pradeho godhūmacūrṇaṃ chagalīpayaśca
natotpalaṃ candanakuṣṭhayuktaṃ śirorujāyāṃ saghṛtaṃ pradehaḥ
lines_deva: वाते सरक्ते सघृतं प्रदेहो गोधूमचूर्णं छगलीपयश्च
नतोत्पलं चन्दनकुष्ठयुक्तं शिरोरुजायां सघृतं प्रदेहः

hindi: प्रपौण्डरीक, सुरदारु, कुष्ठ, यष्टि-नामक (द्रव्य), एला, कमल और उत्पल, तथा लोह, एरका, पद्मक और चोरक के साथ - सिर के दर्द में घृत-सहित प्रदेह (करे)।
english: Prapauṇḍarīka, suradāru, kuṣṭha, the one called yaṣṭi, elā, kamala and utpala, and with loha, erakā, padmaka and coraka: a pradeha with ghee, for headache.

text_flags.why: possible: lodhra is a regular ingredient in such lists and 'loha' as a drug is doubtful; metre does not decide (same syllable count).

notes: The last pāda 'lohairakāpadmakacorakaiḥ ca' is read as loha-erakā-padmaka-coraka (inst. pl.): 'and with loha, erakā, padmaka, coraka'; the sandhi loha+erakā gives 'lohairakā'. The instrumental has no governing verb in the verse; it is read as a further set of ingredients with the preceding list. 'loha' is kept as a name; its sense here is uncertain (possibly an error for lodhra, see text_flags). 'erakā' is not identified. 'yaṣṭyāhva' = 'the one named yaṣṭi' (commonly licorice, but not stated in the verse). 'saghṛtaḥ' is masculine to agree with pradehaḥ.
lines_iast: prapauṇḍarīkaṃ suradāru kuṣṭhaṃ yaṣṭyāhvamelā kamalotpale ca
śirorujāyāṃ saghṛtaḥ pradeho lohairakāpadmakacorakaiśca
lines_deva: प्रपौण्डरीकं सुरदारु कुष्ठं यष्ट्याह्वमेला कमलोत्पले च
शिरोरुजायां सघृतः प्रदेहो लोहैरकापद्मकचोरकैश्च

hindi: रास्ना, दोनों हरिद्रा, नलद, दोनों शताह्वा, देवदारु और मिश्री, जीवन्ती की जड़ - घृत और तेल सहित गुनगुना आलेपन पार्श्व (पसलियों/बगल) के दर्दों में (किया जाए)।
english: Rāsnā, the two haridrās, nalada, the two śatāhvās, the devadārus and sugar-crystal (rock sugar), and the root of jīvantī, with ghee and oil: a lukewarm application (ālepana) for pains in the flank.
notes: 'dve' (f. du.) agrees with 'śatāhve'; 'devadārūṇi' is neuter plural and so cannot take 'dve': read as 'devadārus' in the plural (several kinds of devadāru), not as 'two'; an alternative reading takes 'dve devadārūṇi' as 'two devadārus' (grammatically strained). 'koṣṇa' = ka + uṣṇa = mildly warm. 'ālepanam' (application) is the name of the preparation. Plant names are kept (nalada not identified).
lines_iast: rāsnā haridre naladaṃ śatāhve dve devadārūṇi sitopalā ca
jīvantimūlaṃ saghṛtaṃ satailamālepanaṃ pārśvarujāsu koṣṇam
lines_deva: रास्ना हरिद्रे नलदं शताह्वे द्वे देवदारूणि सितोपला च
जीवन्तिमूलं सघृतं सतैलमालेपनं पार्श्वरुजासु कोष्णम्

hindi: शैवाल, पद्म, उत्पल, वेत्र, तुङ्ग, प्रपौण्डरीक, मृणाल और लोध्र, प्रियङ्गु, कालेयक और चन्दन - घृत सहित यह प्रदेह निर्वापण (शीतल करने वाला) होता है।
english: Śaivāla, padma, utpala, vetra, tuṅga, prapauṇḍarīka, lotus-fibre (mṛṇāla) and lodhra, priyaṅgu, kāleyaka and candana: a pradeha with ghee would be nirvāpaṇa (cooling, quenching).

text_flags.why: Possible error: the extra a- in 'kāṇyamṛṇāla' would be the start of a word 'amṛṇāla' that has no clear meaning; mṛṇāla-lodhra (lotus fibre, lodhra) is the natural reading. Metre does not decide (same syllable count).

notes: The token 'prapauṇḍarīkāṇyamṛṇālalodhram' is irregular. Normal sandhi of 'prapauṇḍarīkāṇi' + 'mṛṇāla...' would be 'prapauṇḍarīkāṇi mṛṇāla...'; the source has an extra a-, giving 'kāṇy-amṛṇāla'. 'amṛṇāla' has no obvious meaning, so a corrupt reading (or a lost word) is possible; the syllable count (22) does not decide, since 'kāṇi mṛ-' and 'kāṇya mṛ-' have the same count. Read as prapauṇḍarīkāṇi + mṛṇāla-lodhram, flagged as possible. 'nirvāpaṇa' = cooling/allaying heat. The plant names are kept unidentified. The reading of mṛṇāla as lotus fibre/stalk is secure.
lines_iast: śaivālapadmotpalavetratuṅgaprapauṇḍarīkāṇyamṛṇālalodhram
priyaṅgukāleyakacandanāni nirvāpaṇaḥ syāt saghṛtaḥ pradehaḥ
lines_deva: शैवालपद्मोत्पलवेत्रतुङ्गप्रपौण्डरीकाण्यमृणाललोध्रम्
प्रियङ्गुकालेयकचन्दनानि निर्वापणः स्यात् सघृतः प्रदेहः

hindi: सितालता, वेतस, पद्मक, यष्टि-नामक (द्रव्य), ऐन्द्री, नलिन (कमल) और दूर्वा, यवास की जड़, कुश और काश की (जड़), जल और एरका - (यह प्रदेह) निर्वापण (शीतल करने वाला) होता है।
english: Sitālatā, vetasa, padmaka, the one called yaṣṭi, aindrī, nalinas (lotuses) and dūrvā grass, the root of yavāsa, of kuśa and of kāśa, water and erakā: [this] would be cooling (nirvāpaṇa).
notes: The verse has no noun for the application ('pradeha' is understood from the neighbouring verses; masculine 'nirvāpaṇaḥ' fits it). 'kuśakāśayoḥ ca' is a dual genitive 'of kuśa and of kāśa'; 'mūlam' is read as the thing governing it (roots). 'jalam' is read as 'water'; it might instead be a drug named jala, not stated. 'sitālatā' may also be split 'sitā-latā'; kept as one name. All plant names except dūrvā (a grass) are left unidentified.
lines_iast: sitālatāvetasapadmakāni yaṣṭyāhvamaindrī nalināni dūrvā
yavāsamūlaṃ kuśakāśayośca nirvāpaṇaḥ syājjalamerakā ca
lines_deva: सितालतावेतसपद्मकानि यष्ट्याह्वमैन्द्री नलिनानि दूर्वा
यवासमूलं कुशकाशयोश्च निर्वापणः स्याज्जलमेरका च

words.gram: n. nom. du. adj. (bahuvrīhi: having kuṣṭha), agreeing with aguruṇī

hindi: शैलेय, एला, कुष्ठ-सहित दोनों अगरु, चण्डा, नत, त्वक्, देवदारु और रास्ना - शीतल प्रदेह शीघ्र विष का नाश करे; और शिरीष सिन्धुवार सहित (नाश करे)।
english: Śaileya, elā, the two agurus together with kuṣṭha, caṇḍā, nata, tvak, suradāru and rāsnā: [applied] cool, the pradeha would quickly destroy poison; and śirīṣa together with sindhuvāra.
notes: Several readings are open. (1) 'aguruṇī' and 'sakuṣṭhe' are dual neuter, so 'the two agurus along with (two) kuṣṭhas'; here taken 'the two agurus, with kuṣṭha'. 'sakuṣṭhe' cannot be a locative singular ('in kuṣṭha disease'), as sa- would not work so. (2) 'śītam' is neuter, so taken adverbially 'cool(ly)' (applied cold); agreement with pradehaḥ would need śītaḥ. (3) 'śirīṣaḥ tu sasindhuvāraḥ' has no verb: it is read as 'and (so also) śirīṣa with sindhuvāra' (viṣaṃ nihanyāt understood); the text could also be read as an independent clause naming the next pradeha. (4) 'tvak' is left as 'tvak' (bark; the drug named tvac). Names (caṇḍā, nata, śaileya) are kept unidentified.
lines_iast: śaileyamelāguruṇī sakuṣṭhe caṇḍā nataṃ tvak suradāru rāsnā
śītaṃ nihanyādacirāt pradeho viṣaṃ śirīṣastu sasindhuvāraḥ
lines_deva: शैलेयमेलागुरुणी सकुष्ठे चण्डा नतं त्वक् सुरदारु रास्ना
शीतं निहन्यादचिरात् प्रदेहो विषं शिरीषस्तु ससिन्धुवारः

hindi: शिरीष, लामज्जक, हेम और लोध्र से (किया हुआ) प्रघर्ष (रगड़ना) त्वचा के दोष और पसीने को हरने वाला है। पत्र, अम्बु, लोध्र, अभया और चन्दन का प्रदेह शरीर की दुर्गन्ध को हरने वाला है।
english: A rubbing (pragharṣa) with śirīṣa, lāmajjaka, hema and lodhra removes skin disorders and sweating; a pradeha of patra, ambu, lodhra, abhaya and candana removes body odour.
notes: 'tvak-doṣa-saṃsveda-hara' is read as a dvandva-like tat-puruṣa 'remover of skin disorders and sweating'; 'removes sweat-related skin defects' is another possible reading. 'saṃsveda' is plain 'sweating'. Drug names are kept (patra = leaf, ambu = water or the drug named ambu, hema = gold or a plant, abhaya = harītakī in common use; the verse does not say). Two items (lodhra) occur in both halves.
lines_iast: śirīṣalāmajjakahemalodhraistvagdoṣasaṃsvedaharaḥ pragharṣaḥ
patrāmbulodhrābhayacandanāni śarīradaurgandhyaharaḥ pradehaḥ
lines_deva: शिरीषलामज्जकहेमलोध्रैस्त्वग्दोषसंस्वेदहरः प्रघर्षः
पत्राम्बुलोध्राभयचन्दनानि शरीरदौर्गन्ध्यहरः प्रदेहः

hindi: इस आरग्वधीय (अध्याय) में सिद्धों और महर्षियों से पूजनीय आत्रेय ने जगत् के हित के लिए अनेक रोगों का नाश करने वाले बत्तीस अत्यन्त सिद्ध (सुप्रमाणित) चूर्ण-प्रदेह कहे हैं।
english: Here, in the Āragvadhīya, Ātreya, revered by siddhas and great sages, has declared for the benefit of the world thirty-two most effective powder pradehas, destroyers of various diseases.
notes: 'siddhatamān' (acc. pl., 'most proven/effective') is construed with 'cūrṇapradehān' in the second line. 'dvātriṃśatam' (acc. sg.) is a collective numeral standing in apposition to the plural noun (construction as 'the thirty-two'). 'siddhamaharṣipūjyaḥ' = 'revered by siddhas and great sages' (dvandva of siddha and maharṣi); the other reading, 'revered by perfected great sages' (siddha as adjective of maharṣi), is also possible. 'iha' = here, in this chapter/discussion; 'āragvadhīye' = in the Āragvadhīya. The lead-in 'tatra ślokaḥ' is singular although two lines follow.
lines_iast: ihātrijaḥ siddhatamānuvāca dvātriṃśataṃ siddhamaharṣipūjyaḥ
cūrṇapradehān vividhāmayaghnānāragvadhīye jagato hitārtham
lines_deva: इहात्रिजः सिद्धतमानुवाच द्वात्रिंशतं सिद्धमहर्षिपूज्यः
चूर्णप्रदेहान् विविधामयघ्नानारग्वधीये जगतो हितार्थम्
